chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Amr ibn Nuhayk, the seller of the Harawis, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O My believing servant, I do not turn away anything from you except that I make it better for you. So let him be pleased with My decree, and let him be patient with My trials, and let him be grateful for My bounties. I shall write him, O Muhammad, as one of the truthful (siddiqun) in My presence.'

key_terms.لَا أَصْرِفُهُ: I do not turn away/convert it

ai.seo_question: What does God promise to the believer regarding His decree and trials?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith qudsi emphasizes the Shia concept of 'husn al-zann' (good opinion of God) by assuring believers that divine decree is inherently beneficial, even when perceived as hardship. It links the spiritual station of 'siddiqun' (the truthful) directly to the triad of satisfaction (rida), patience (sabr), and gratitude (shukr), reflecting the theological balance between divine will and human agency. This narration serves as a cornerstone for understanding how trials are not merely tests but transformative mechanisms for elevating the soul's proximity to God.
